entry_points.text: Build long-term mounts from type names with internal ownership and consume rooted post-parse contexts into attachable mounts.
Bootstrap async caches, mount internal pseudo filesystem aborting boot on failure, then create request and context caches with controls.
Release superblock activity, create anon inodes, release files anywhere, tear down async state on exit.

exports.text: Take dentry refs, queue zero-count entries for tail drain, defer last file close via task or delayed work with separate backing teardown.
Report aggregate mount refs and writers, allocate records with cover/id/name, assign unique ids, attach roots, turn rooted contexts into mounts.
Acquire mount roots once with born publish and checks, drop unusable roots, release activity then passive refs with deferred destruction.
Allocate mount contexts with creds and namespaces, parse monolithic options with fallback, build long-term internal mounts.
Mint pseudo inodes with fresh numbers, set restricted pseudo contexts, bootstrap async caches, register cancel callbacks, tear down on exit.
Set and truncate stamps to superblock range/granularity, refresh ctime with coarse/fine choice, init inodes, mappings and locks.

hazards.text: Warn on remaining writers and lingering state; success without root is fatal; missing block linkage and negative max size warn only.
Clamp stamps and warn on bad config; wait pins uninterruptibly; validate remap identity, liveness and size.
Use doomed and internal markers with kernel tags plus shrink and coverage markers to pick sync versus deferred destroy and direct free.
Restrict pseudo with ring identity and use private anon modes; keep mount, async, file, mapping and error vocabularies fixed.
Use per-CPU inode batches, nanosecond granularity checks, mount versus submount versus reconfigure purposes, unit delayed scheduling, and page-derived ring capacities with first-page offset.
Rely on external spin and semaphore locks, RCU, atomics, irq save, lists, per-CPU access, folio, alloc, error-pointer, warning and debug helpers owned elsewhere.

invariants.text: Teardown once via zero count and doomed; MP scans releases first; new mounts get cover, unique id, fallback name, one ref, null map, fixed links, pinned super/root.
Pair shrink flags with accounting; free mountpoints only when lists empty, clearing mounted state and moving dentry to shrink list with RCU release.
Publish death once under lock with wakeup; context teardown reverses root, state, security, namespaces, creds, log and storage with last-user log free.
Anon numbers avoid zero with batches; ctime tries coarse then fine with atomic swap and queried handling; truncation clamps range and granularity, warns on bad config.
Select file teardown by mode: unopened non-backing frees at once, skip accounting only when marked, backing uses separate cache with path release.
Size rings with margin and dual headers; bound doubled capacity safely; batch per-CPU credits with CAS refill; reuse table holes, quadruple when full with deferred free.

locks.text: Serialize mount hash and id changes with sequence write lock, short id-map guard, read guard for publish, and super write-guard drop after tree success.
Require per-dentry spin lock for shrink queueing, unqueueing and mountpoint transfer.
Use exclusive semaphore for last superblock activity, global spin lock for unlink and dead publish, unlocking when activity reappears else destroying.
Pair RCU read protection with per-pin wait lock for completion and waiters; init mappings with semaphores, private and migration locks plus optional size sequencing.
Layer migration spin guard, setup mutex with try-acquire, completion guard for pointer swap, table lock plus RCU for growth and remap, irq save for cancel and credits.

state_machines.text: Move mount counted to doomed to detached to destroyed with sync or deferred path; cleanup drains pins, notifies, releases root and super, erases id, frees via RCU; pin kill waits.
Drain shrink lists from tail under lock, freeing killed entries at once, otherwise following chained killing until empty.
Move superblock counting to exclusive check, unlocking when busy else notifying death and freeing via RCU with type last.
Move context empty to rooted to mounted; reject rooted acquisition, publish born state, discard root on security failure, consume root once into mount and drop guard.
Free unopened non-backing files at once, defer normal closes to thread task work, queue interrupt, kernel-thread or post-exit closes to shared delayed work.
Move async alloc to live, termination with unmap, user drain with cancel, request drain with wait, deferred reclaim; migrate folios after liveness, guard and index checks with locked swap.

structs.text: Mount carries namespace, flags, root, superblock, links, ids, per-CPU counts, expiry and child lists, cover, pins, notify, name, map and deferred state.
Dentry shrink view carries reusable linkage, lock with count and membership flags; mountpoint adds hash, lists, back pointer and RCU state.

Superblock holds counts, flags, links, mounts, namespaces, device and wake handling; context holds purpose, type, creds, namespaces, root, ops, data, security, source and log with pseudo restrictions.
Inode/mapping hold number, mode, ownership, state, superblock, tree with locks, lists, hash and sequencing; async wraps inode with context and lock.

Async context holds liveness, id, mapping, ring, folios, dual capacities, accounting, credits, lists, waits, dual refs, deferred free; bindings pair alloc/free with stats and VM, file and mapping ops.
